events.title: A Lone Survivor Reaches Jalalabad
events.description: Assistant Surgeon William Brydon rode, wounded, up to the walls of Jalalabad in Afghanistan. He was the only European to reach the garrison from the British army that had left Kabul a week earlier. Of the roughly 16,000 soldiers and camp followers who set out, almost none made it.
events.significance: The retreat from Kabul was one of the worst defeats of the British Empire in the 19th century. It became a lasting warning about foreign intervention in Afghanistan.

events.title: Zola Publishes "J'accuse"
events.description: Novelist Émile Zola printed an open letter to French President Félix Faure on the front page of the newspaper L'Aurore under the headline "J'accuse...!". He accused the army and the government of wrongly convicting Captain Alfred Dreyfus and of covering up the truth.
events.significance: The letter turned the Dreyfus Affair into a national crisis. It became a landmark in the history of press freedom, intellectual activism and the fight against antisemitism.

events.title: Mickey Mouse Comes to the Comics
events.description: The Mickey Mouse newspaper comic strip debuted, distributed by King Features Syndicate. Ub Iwerks drew the first month of the strip. It brought the cartoon star from the movie screen to daily newspapers.
events.significance: It was among the first Disney comics and ran for more than 65 years, until 1995. It helped establish Mickey as a multimedia icon.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in Vilnius
events.description: On January 13, Soviet forces carried out the bloodiest day of repression in the January Events in Lithuania. Civilians who supported the country's restored independence were met with violence around the Vilnius television tower. The events ran from January 11 to 13.
events.significance: Lithuania held on to its independence and Soviet forces withdrew from the cities. Lithuanians now mark January 13 as the Day of the Defenders of Freedom.
